You are implementing performance round 7 for zarrow, a Zig-native Apache Arrow library. Three targets: (A) concat of dictionary arrays whose parts have different dictionaries (the last UnsupportedType in concatArrayRefs) via dictionary unification; (B) measure and speed up UTF-8 validation inside validateFull for string/large_string/string_view arrays; (C) measure dictionary encoding (building a dictionary array from values) and speed it up if it is far from arrow-rs class (~10-20 ns/row for int/short strings). Deliver a patch plus notes; do not touch the original worktree.

## Setup
- Source repo (read only for you): C:\Users\cable\Documents\dev\zarrow\.claude\worktrees\zig-0-17-migration-branch-f92e21, HEAD ebfce9d (round 6 merged). Work in a short scratch path: create C:\Users\cable\AppData\Local\Temp\fz7 (delete if present), fill with `git -C <repo> archive HEAD | tar -x -C <fz7>`, `git init` + commit inside so you can diff. Make a base copy C:\Users\cable\AppData\Local\Temp\fz7b for A/B. Deep paths break link.exe and git on Windows: stay in those short dirs.
- Zig 0.17 = `zig` on PATH. Zig 0.16 = `C:\Users\cable\tools\zig-x86_64-windows-0.16.0\zig.exe` always with `--cache-dir .zig-cache16`. NEVER run both compilers at once (shared global cache). Always `-j2`; a zstd vendor compile flake happens occasionally, retry once. Code must compile on both: no `@backingInt/@fromBackingInt`, no 0.17-only std APIs. CI lint is 0.16 `zig fmt`. The fz7 tree is LF, keep it LF.
- Bash heredocs with big bodies fail on this machine: use the Write tool for files. Benchmarks: `zig build benchmark-<name>_benchmark -Doptimize=ReleaseFast -j2`, one at a time, machine noisy; alternate base/new runs for A/B (scratchpad ab4.sh is a harness you may copy). build.zig registers every benchmarks/*_benchmark.zig automatically; new CSV names must be added to tools/benchmark_ci_check.py EXPECTED_BENCHES, tools/benchmark_ci_thresholds.json and tools/test_benchmark_ci_check.py VALID_ROWS.
- Scratchpad for deliverables: C:\Users\cable\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-cable-Documents-dev-zarrow--claude-worktrees-zig-0-17-migration-branch-f92e21\3ab19c71-6c26-4cbd-ba49-bd6ba48132fc\scratchpad\ . Read perf4_notes.md, perf5_notes.md, perf6_notes.md there first: they document concatManyFlat (the dictionary arm returns null when dictionaries differ), Part windows, concatParts, the take kernels, the oracle test `rowsEqual` in src/compute/test_datum.zig and the concat oracle test you extend.

## (A) Dictionary unification in concat (src/concat_array_refs.zig)
- When dictionary parts do not share one dictionary node: build one merged dictionary (values of the first dictionary, then each new distinct value of the next ones, in first-seen order; a hash map keyed on the value bytes for string/binary, on the fixed-width bytes for primitives; values with nulls: a null dictionary entry maps to one shared null slot), build an index remap table per part (old index -> new index), then gather the indices (null index rows stay null). If the merged dictionary does not fit the index type (e.g. > 255 for uint8/int8 indices) return error.InvalidInput (do not silently widen the index type: the result type must equal the requested type). Reject out-of-range indices in a part (index >= that part's dictionary length) as InvalidInput: parts may come from hostile IPC data. Reuse zarrow's existing hashing/dictionary-builder code if there is one (look in src/ for dictionary builders / unifiers before writing a hash map; `std.StringHashMap` / `std.HashMap` with a byte-slice key is fine otherwise). Validate the result with validateLayout as the other paths do. Dictionaries that already share one node keep the existing fast path.
- Also handle the chunked-take fallback in src/compute/datum_permutation.zig takeChunked: today, when chunks have different dictionaries, concat-first fails and the per-run path is used; keep that (it is still correct and avoids a unification), but make sure a chunked filter / takeAsArray on dictionary chunks with different dictionaries now returns one array (it concatenates the pieces at the end and that concat now unifies).
- Benchmark: add `concat_nested_dictionary` to benchmarks/concat_nested_benchmark.zig: 12,500 parts × 16 rows of dictionary<int32, string>, every part with its own 16-value dictionary where half the values repeat across parts. Target < 30 ns/row (hash per distinct value per part, not per row).
- Tests: extend the concat oracle test with differing-dictionary parts (full, sliced, empty part, nulls in indices and in dictionary values), result validateFull and rows equal to source rows through rowsEqual (which resolves dictionary values); index-type overflow rejected; out-of-range index rejected; chunked filter over differing-dictionary chunks returns one array matching the flat filter.

## (B) UTF-8 validation in validateFull
- Find where validateFull checks string validity (src/array/array_data.zig or wherever `utf8` appears) and add a benchmark `validate_full_string` (200k rows of ~16-byte ASCII strings with occasional multi-byte chars) to a new benchmarks/validate_benchmark.zig with cases `validate_full_string` and `validate_full_int32_list` (the structural checks only). Measure first. If UTF-8 validation is > ~0.5 ns/byte, speed it up: validate the whole data range once (not per row: the Arrow rule is that the concatenation of all valid strings is valid UTF-8 only if each string is; the common fast path is: validate the entire [first offset, last offset) byte range once with std.unicode.utf8ValidateSlice or a 16/32-lane @Vector ASCII fast path that falls back to the scalar validator for non-ASCII blocks; per-row boundaries only need re-checking at offsets where a string starts in the middle of a multi-byte sequence: check that every offset points at a non-continuation byte, which is one byte load per row). Null rows' bytes do not need validation (but keep it simple: validating them too is acceptable if the range is contiguous, as long as hostile bytes in null slots cannot make a valid array fail validation. Arrow C++ validates only non-null slots; check the existing behaviour and tests and keep it).
- Keep validation strength identical or stronger (never accept something validateFull rejects today). Target: string validateFull < 0.3 ns/byte for ASCII-heavy data.

## (C) Dictionary encoding
- Find the dictionary builder / encode kernel (grep for `dictionary` in src/array/*builder* and src/compute/). Add `dictionary_encode_string` and `dictionary_encode_int32` cases (200k rows, 1,000 distinct values) to a new benchmarks/dictionary_benchmark.zig. Measure. If > 30 ns/row, improve: reserve capacity up front, hash the bytes once with std.hash.Wyhash, avoid per-row allocations, build the index buffer directly. If no encode kernel exists, add a minimal one (`dictionaryEncode(allocator, array) -> ArrayRef` for string/binary and fixed-width inputs) next to the existing builders, nothing more.

## Rules
- ponytail: smallest working code, reuse what exists, no new abstractions; every path keeps bounds checks; never loosen validation at trust boundaries (IPC/C-ABI decoded data feeds concat and validateFull; the fuzz compute/array-layout targets exercise them).
- Verify on the final code: `zig build test -j2` on both compilers, `zig build fuzz-corpus -j2` on both, 0.16 fmt clean on touched files, `python -I tools/test_benchmark_ci_check.py`, and `python tools/fuzz.py --optimize ReleaseSafe --out .fuzz-out run --targets compute,array-layout,ipc-stream --seconds 180` on fz7 (a `hang | |` with no frames on c-abi is a known load artifact; anything else is a finding to fix; a reproducer goes in fuzz/corpus/<dir>/regress-<8 hex>.bin).
- Deliverables: `<scratchpad>\perf7.patch` (LF, `git apply --check` must pass against a `git archive HEAD` tree of ebfce9d, including new files) and `<scratchpad>\perf7_notes.md` (per target: measurement before, root cause, design, trust boundaries, tests, before/after table, what was skipped and why). Final report: 10 lines max plus the table.

take the higher one and move on. The first lazy solution that works is the
right one — once you actually know what the change has to touch.

edit, grep every caller of the function you're about to touch. The lazy fix IS

every sibling caller still broken. Fix it once, where all callers route through.

- No boilerplate, no scaffolding "for later", later can scaffold for itself.

| Level | What change |
